_doc: Who holds which wpss_* capability, and what each one AUTHORISES.
The scope field is the point. A WordPress capability name does not say whether it
means 'your own' or 'anyone's', and reading one the wrong way is a privilege
escalation. That is not hypothetical here: the FluentCart order routes gated on
wpss_manage_services, which READS like a site-wide management power and is granted
to every vendor at registration. Behind it sat an unscoped SELECT * over every order
on the marketplace, so any self-registered vendor could read every buyer's billing
own     - authorises the CALLER'S OWN object only. Never sufficient on its own in a
permission callback; pair it with an ownership comparison.
any     - authorises acting on anyone's object. The real site-wide authority.
feature - 'may use this feature at all'. Fine as a bare entry gate where no object
exists yet (creating one, listing your own).
CapabilityMapTest fails when a capability exists in a role but not here, when this
file names one no role holds, and when a wpss_* capability is checked bare in source
without being allow-listed with a reason.

wpss_vendor.means: This account is a vendor. A marker, not an authority - it never decides access to a specific object.
wpss_vendor.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

wpss_manage_services.means: May create and manage THE CALLER'S OWN services. Despite the name, this is NOT a site-wide management power and NOT an admin capability.
wpss_manage_services.warning: Every vendor holds this from registration (Core/Activator.php, Services/VendorService.php). Any gate that uses it to mean 'staff' is a privilege escalation - that is exactly what happened on the FluentCart routes (Basecamp 10321653293). The site-wide equivalents are edit_others_wpss_services and wpss_manage_orders.
wpss_manage_services.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

wpss_view_analytics.means: May view THE CALLER'S OWN analytics. Not marketplace-wide figures.
wpss_view_analytics.warning: Every vendor holds this. The Pro wpss/analytics-overview ability gated marketplace-wide analytics on it and was saved only by the inner route's admin check (Basecamp 10321653478, finding 6). Marketplace-wide analytics require manage_options.
wpss_view_analytics.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

wpss_vendor_orders.means: May act on orders where the caller is the VENDOR. Ownership is still compared separately; this only says the caller is a seller at all.
wpss_vendor_orders.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

wpss_respond_to_requests.means: May submit proposals to buyer requests. No object exists at the point this is checked.
wpss_respond_to_requests.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

wpss_manage_orders.means: Site staff authority over ANY order, including forcing a status transition the state machine would refuse.
wpss_manage_orders.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

wpss_manage_disputes.means: Site staff authority over ANY dispute: mediate, resolve, refund.
wpss_manage_disputes.note: Deliberately NOT granted to shop_manager, unlike wpss_manage_orders.

wpss_manage_vendors.means: Approve, suspend and edit ANY vendor profile.

wpss_manage_settings.means: Plugin configuration. Paired with manage_options at every call site.

edit_wpss_services.means: Standard WordPress CPT capability over the caller's OWN wpss_service posts. Held by every vendor.
edit_wpss_services.held_by_note: shop_manager is WooCommerce's role, not ours. Activator.php grants the staff set to it only when the role exists, so on a site without WooCommerce it holds nothing.

The forcing is audited downstream via can_transition_naturally() -> AuditLogService, so forensics can tell a forced transition from a natural one.

bare_check_allowlist.src/Core/AbilitiesRegistrar.php:490: Entry gate on wpss/request-withdrawal. Delegates to POST /earnings/withdrawals, which scopes to the caller.
